comments.note: getCacheFolder() path mismatch: Comic::getCacheFolder() returns {comicFolder}/cache, but Fetcher constructs FetchCache with $this->folder (= comic->getStorageFolder() = {comicFolder}/downloaded), placing the actual cache at {comicFolder}/downloaded/cache. If WP-003 or UI code calls getCacheFolder() to display or manage cache files, it will reference the wrong directory. Before WP-003 proceeds, either: (a) change getCacheFolder() to return getStorageFolder()+'/cache', or (b) change the Fetcher constructor to use $this->comic->getCacheFolder() instead of $this->folder. Option (b) is preferable since it makes the intent of getCacheFolder() explicit and keeps Fetcher aligned with the Comic API.

FetchCache::put() writes the HTML file with a bare file_put_contents(), which is not atomic. If the process dies mid-write, the manifest will contain a reference to a corrupt/partial .html file, causing the next get() to return garbage. Consider writing to a temp file and renaming (the same pattern JSONFile uses for the manifest) to make HTML writes safe too. Risk is low for a local-only tool, but worth addressing in a follow-up.

FetchCache::get() accepts a $url parameter that is not used in the read path (only put() stores the URL into the manifest). The parameter exists on get() for API symmetry, but passing a URL on every read is noisy and can mislead callers into thinking the URL participates in cache lookup. Consider either removing $url from get() or adding a short doc comment clarifying it is ignored on reads.
